🧠  Aberrations (Creature Type)
Aberrations are not errors of emotion or echoes of destruction—they are living miscalculations. Born 
from paradoxes, flawed experiments, recursive loops, or collapsed causal structures, these beings violate 
the logical foundations of reality. They do not just defy understanding—they invert it.
🧬  Origin

publishedSample.heading: Aberrations emerge from
publishedSample.text:
•Broken timelines
•Overloaded conceptual fields
•Fractal regressions
•Synthetic simulations gone rogue
•Mathematical truths that became sentient

publishedSample.heading: They often appear in places where reality folded in on itself, such as
publishedSample.text:
•Failed portals
•Forbidden laboratories
•Abandoned megastructures
•Zones of unstable time

Aberrations come with their own mechanical expectations, distinct from other monster types.
🧠  Mental Strain
Aberrations trigger mental strain when first perceived or interacted with directly:
•Trigger: Entering sensory range or initiating direct interaction (combat, speech, etc.)
•Save: DC 16 Intelligence or Wisdom (playerʼs choice)
•Failure Effect: Confused (1 round), or disadvantage on Logic-based skill checks vs the aberration 
(duration: 1 minute)
Mental strain represents the logical dissonance caused by trying to comprehend an impossible form.

🧩  Campaign Use
Aberration encounters should not be standard fights—theyʼre logic puzzles wrapped in violence.

publishedSample.heading: Recommended uses include
publishedSample.text:
•Distorted Dungeons
Aberrations may lair in impossible towers or recursive caves. Rooms may repeat, reflect, or rearrange.
•Investigation Hooks
Clues may include fractured equations, dreams of impossible shapes, or witnesses repeating phrases 
in foreign logic.
•Philosophical Arcs
Use Aberrations to question the nature of reality, causality, time, or perception. They may serve 
unknowable masters—or be the broken echo of one.
•Reality Breaches
Their appearance may signal instability in the local timeline or multiverse structure. Repeated 
appearances may precede a Collapse Event or Resync Protocol.
🧪  Aberration Subtypes

publishedSample.heading: Aberrations may fall into one or more of the following designations
publishedSample.text:
•Causal Aberrations – distort time and event chains
•Fractal Aberrations – self-replicating, recursive
•Cognitive Aberrations – attack perception and memory
•Conceptual Aberrations – embody failed ideas
•Geometric Aberrations – break or feed on space
•Synthetic Aberrations – emergent from corrupted code or AI
•Temporal Aberrations – manipulate time directly
Each subtype grants unique traits referenced in stat blocks.

This weighting allows frequent low-level appearances for strange and mysterious encounters, while high-
CR aberrations can function as campaign-disrupting entities or final bosses.
📚  Integration Tips (GM Advice)
•Donʼt explain everything. The fear and allure of aberrations is rooted in mystery. Let players theorize.
•Change the rules slightly. Let aberration zones ignore some player assumptions. For example: “You 
cast fireball, but it travels backward and strikes your starting square.”
•Use math as flavor. Describe the terrain as "folded at 73° angles” or enemies as "defined by a 
recursive Mandelbrot pattern."
